name: Arulmigu Samayapuram Mariamman Temple
deity: The Goddess as Mariamman, giver of health and rain
period: A great Mariamman shrine near the Kaveri by Tiruchirapalli, sought for healing and vows
summary: Near the Kaveri by Tiruchirapalli, the Goddess is worshipped as Samayapuram Mariamman — the mother sought for health and for the fulfilment of vows, one of the most visited Amman temples in the Tamil country.

sections.history: Samayapuram stands a little north of Tiruchirapalli, near the Kaveri. Here the Goddess is worshipped as Mariamman, the folk mother associated with health, rain, and the curing of disease. Grown from the Vijayanagara and Nayak period, it is among the wealthiest and most visited temples in Tamil Nadu, drawing crowds for its vows and healing.
sections.architecture: The temple is built in the Dravidian manner around the shrine of the Goddess, who is worshipped in a form of raw power rather than gentle grace. Its precincts fill with devotees fulfilling vows, and its festival processions are among the largest in the region.
sections.legends: Mariamman is the mother of the village and the fields, sought especially against the pox and fevers, and Samayapuram's Goddess is held to be swift to answer such prayers. Devotees make offerings of many kinds — rolling around the shrine, carrying fire-pots, shaving the head — in fulfilment of vows made in distress.
sections.festivals: The Chithirai Thiruvizha is the great festival, when the Goddess is drawn in procession and vast crowds come from across the Tamil country. Fridays and the Tamil month of Aadi are especially thronged.
sections.experience: Samayapuram is a temple of the vow and its fulfilment — a place of intense, direct devotion, where the mother is petitioned in trouble and thanked in relief, amid some of the largest crowds of the Kaveri country.

visit.timings: Open daily from early morning to night; Fridays, the month of Aadi, and the Chithirai festival are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Samayapuram lies on the Tiruchirapalli–Chennai road a little north of Tiruchirapalli in Tamil Nadu, easily reached by road, with Tiruchirapalli the nearest major rail and air hub.
